record.paper_title: Open Questions in CMR Manganites, Relevance of Clustered States, and Analogies with other Compounds
record.original_question: How important is the antiferromagnetic Heisenberg coupling JAF between localized t2g spins for stabilizing A-type, CE-type, and charge-stacked states in manganites, and are there alternative microscopic mechanisms that can stabilize those phases if JAF is not the whole explanation?

evidence.quote: Is the "small" JAF coupling between localized t2g spins truly an important coupling for manganites? ... Are there alternative mechanisms for stabilization of A-, CE- and charge stacking states?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a two-orbital double-exchange model for manganites of the form
H = -∑⟨ij⟩,αβ,σ t^{αβ}_{ij} c†_{iασ} c_{jβσ} - J_H ∑_i s_i · S_i + J_AF ∑_⟨ij⟩ S_i · S_j + H_{JT}+ H_{Coul},
where c_{iασ} annihilates an e_g electron of orbital α∈{d_{x²-y²}, d_{3z²-r²}} and spin σ at site i on a cubic lattice, S_i is a localized t_{2g} spin (treated classically, |S_i|=3/2), s_i is the e_g spin density at i, J_H ≫ |t| is the Hund coupling, J_AF > 0 is the nearest-neighbour antiferromagnetic Heisenberg coupling between localized t_{2g} spins, H_{JT} is the cooperative Jahn–Teller coupling of e_g electrons to Q_2, Q_3 distortions of the MnO_6 octahedra, and H_{Coul} contains on-site and nearest-neighbour Coulomb repulsions.

The "A-type" antiferromagnetic state (ferromagnetic xy planes stacked antiferromagnetically along z), the "CE-type" state at hole density x=1/2 (zigzag ferromagnetic chains with checkerboard charge order, antiferromagnetically stacked), and "charge-stacked" states (planes of identical charge density alternating along z) are well-known ordered phases observed in manganites such as La_{1-x}Ca_xMnO_3 and related compounds.

Address the following:

(a) Within the above model, is a nonzero antiferromagnetic Heisenberg coupling J_AF between localized t_{2g} spins necessary to stabilize the A-type, CE-type, and charge-stacked phases as ground states in the appropriate doping ranges? Determine, as quantitatively as possible, the minimal J_AF/t required (or prove that J_AF can be set to zero) for each of these three phases to be the ground state in the relevant region of the phase diagram.

(b) Identify alternative microscopic mechanisms — for example, cooperative Jahn–Teller distortions, nearest-neighbour Coulomb repulsion V, orbital ordering, or electron–phonon couplings beyond the breathing mode — that, in the limit J_AF → 0, can by themselves stabilize each of the A-type, CE-type, and charge-stacked phases. For each phase, decide whether such an alternative mechanism exists and, if so, exhibit it.
artifact.category_tag: strongly correlated electron models for manganites
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has shown that Jahn–Teller distortions and nearest-neighbour Coulomb repulsion can play a major role in stabilizing CE-type charge ordering at half doping, and Monte Carlo studies of one- and two-orbital models with cooperative phonons explore the interplay with J_AF. However, no consensus quantitative answer specifying the minimal J_AF needed for A-, CE- and charge-stacked phases, nor a complete classification of alternative mechanisms, appears to have been established; the question remains an open modeling problem.

status_evidence.title: Jahn-Teller distortion induced charge-ordering in CE phase of half-doped manganites
status_evidence.snippet: The charge order of the CE phase in half-doped manganites is caused by Jahn-Teller distortions of MnO6 octahedra rather than Coulomb repulsion.
status_evidence.claim: Alternative (Jahn–Teller) mechanism for CE-phase stabilization is supported, but the role of J_AF is not eliminated.

status_evidence.title: Competing Ferromagnetic and Charge-Ordered States in Models for Manganites
status_evidence.snippet: One-orbital model with cooperative phonons and superexchange coupling JAF investigated via Monte Carlo; competition near a bicritical point yields CMR.
status_evidence.claim: J_AF remains an essential ingredient in current Monte Carlo studies of manganite phase competition, indicating the question of its necessity is not fully resolved.
